tagline.text: A Shrine to St. Joseph and a Modern Church in Greenhills

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of Duke and Buffalo Streets, East Greenhills, Mandaluyong

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0–500 (half day, including transport and snacks)

children.text: Santuario de San Jose is a shrine church to St. Joseph built in the 1960s on land donated by the Ortigas Company. Set in the East Greenhills residential area, it is quiet, and its modern building, stained glass and daily Masses are the main draw. It pairs well with a visit to Greenhills Shopping Center.

Santuario de San Jose is a church of the Archdiocese of Manila dedicated to St. Joseph (San Jose), the foster father of Jesus, and designated as a shrine to him. The word "Santuario" in its official name means a shrine church that gathers devotion to St. Joseph. Its address is the corner of Duke and Buffalo Streets in East Greenhills, and most sources place it in Mandaluyong City. OpenStreetMap, however, marks it on the San Juan side, since it sits close to the boundary of the two cities, and among Koreans in Manila it is simply called the "Greenhills church."

The church dates from the 1960s. As Greenhills was being developed, the Ortigas Company donated about 5,030 sq m of hilly land to the Archdiocese of Manila, and Fr. Guido Colletti of the Oblates of St. Joseph (OSJ) raised funds and began construction in March 1964. The work took about 25 months, and the church was consecrated on April 2, 1966, with a seminary and rectory built behind it. It was formally established as a parish in 1967; sources give the date as either April 17 or April 19. The first parishioners numbered about 3,500, drawn from the Wack-Wack and White Plains subdivisions and the area around Camp Crame. Before the building was fully finished in 1966, the Misa de Gallo (the pre-Christmas dawn Masses) and Sunday Masses were reportedly held in the unfinished church. These details follow Wikipedia and are old records, so it is best to confirm specifics with the parish.

The appeal of this place as a destination is not grand monuments but a close look at everyday life in a modern Philippine city church. The architect was Manuel Mañosa Jr., with Nemesio Montenegro handling the structure. Its hallmarks are a plain modern exterior, an interior of gold and wood finishes, and stained glass that filters the light. A small garden near the entrance has a grotto where you can rest for a while. Because it stands inside a residential subdivision, there is little vendor or heavy traffic noise, and it is within walking distance of Greenhills Shopping Center, so it fits well into a half-day outing around shopping.

Keep in mind that this is a working parish, not a tourist facility. During Mass, worshippers come first, so be careful with noise and photography. The parish priests are assigned by the Oblates of St. Joseph, and the parish also oversees the Holy Family Chapel inside Greenhills Shopping Center and two chapels in Crame, San Juan. Wikipedia says the parish has more than 100,000 members, while another source says more than 50,000, so the exact number is uncertain. The parish's history is also preserved in the names of its priests. According to Wikipedia, Fr. Guido Colletti served as the first parish priest until 1989, and Fr. Constantino Conti took over in June 1989. Fr. Colletti died in November 1996, and several Oblates of St. Joseph priests, including Fr. Napoleon Jinon, have served as parish priest since. The years in Wikipedia's table do not fully match its text, so exact terms are not stated here. For travelers, this story offers background: a church that a local community has built up over nearly 60 years.
The parish feast is celebrated on
March 19

, the Solemnity of St. Joseph. St. Joseph Marello and the Sacred Heart of Jesus are also secondary patrons of the parish. Around the feast, Masses and events increase and the church is busier than usual.

Architect Manuel Mañosa Jr. designed the church and Nemesio Montenegro handled the structure. It is a semi-concrete building of sand, gravel, cement, mortar and steel, with a seminary and rectory built together behind it. It is interesting to compare with older Spanish-style churches.

The interior uses gold and wood finishes, and stained glass depicting Jesus filters the sunlight. The center aisle is described as having a red carpet and chandeliers, along with a balcony. The altar and aisle are neat and good for photos, but avoid taking them during Mass.

blocks.title: Bell tower and St. Joseph image

children.text: The church has a bell tower and sanctuary, and images of St. Joseph with the Child Jesus and of the Santo Entierro (Holy Burial) are mentioned. Little is documented about the details of the images, so please see them in person.

blocks.title: The grotto in the entrance garden

children.text: A small garden near the entrance has a grotto where you can sit and rest for a moment. According to a wedding-guide website, there is also a wide parking area and a driveway leading to the entrance. However, some reviews say parking is tight on busy days.
Weekday Masses are at
and

, and there are several Masses on Sundays. The morning Mass is livestreamed on Facebook. The Wednesday evening Mass is a votive Mass to St. Joseph and the Friday evening Mass is a votive Mass to the Holy Family.

Being inside East Greenhills, it is relatively removed from street vendors and main-road noise. You can enjoy a calm atmosphere in contrast to the bustle of Greenhills Shopping Center. Since it is a residential area, keep your voice down as you walk the lanes as well.
Arrive at the corner of Duke and Buffalo Streets in East Greenhills and look around the entrance garden and the grotto.
If no Mass is under way, go inside and take your time with the stained glass, the altar and the image of St. Joseph. If Mass is on, attend quietly at the back or wait in the garden.
Ask about the church's history and events at the parish office or nearby. Office hours are unconfirmed, so call to find out.
Head toward Greenhills Shopping Center for lunch and shopping. One source says the jeepney stop is about
1 minute
on foot from the church, but confirm on site.
Mass schedules can change, so check the parish's latest announcements before you visit.

items.title: Mass route
items.subtitle: Wednesday evening votive Mass to St. Joseph

children.text: On Wednesdays, confession is reported to be held from
. Arrive early to get a feel for the church.
Attend the votive Mass to St. Joseph. You can sit quietly even if you are not a believer.
After Mass, have dinner on the Greenhills side.
Look at the lines and colors of the modern exterior from outside. Its hallmark is its sparse decoration and simple lines.
Walk around the bell tower, the entrance garden and the grotto. The garden is described as a good spot for photos.
When no Mass is being held, look up at the stained glass, the gold decoration and the balcony inside.
Head to the shopping center for a snack and end the day there.
Little is documented about the specific designs of the stained glass or when the images were made. Ask the parish on site.
From Manila (Malate, Ermita, Makati), you can take the MRT-3 toward Santolan and then continue by jeepney, taxi or Grab into East Greenhills. Check routes and transfers on a map app.
According to Moovit, the nearest station is MRT-3 Santolan (about 1 km), about
14 minutes
on foot, and LRT-2 Betty Go-Belmonte is about 3 km away, roughly
40 minutes
on foot. Rome2Rio also lists the Santolan station to Greenhills walk at about 1.1 km and 13 minutes, but check the actual time on a map app.
A jeepney stop for Gate 5–Unimart and Greenhills Shopping Center routes is reported on Missouri Street, in front of Greenhills Promenade Mall.
When leaving from Manila, allow
1 hour
or more and avoid rush hours.
Routes and fares change often, so check a map app and confirm on site.
The simplest way is to enter the destination as "Santuario de San Jose, corner of Duke and Buffalo Streets, East Greenhills" when booking.
City traffic is heavy, so avoid rush hours.

items.title: On foot from Greenhills Shopping Center

children.text: You can walk from the shopping center toward East Greenhills. Check the exact route on a map app.
Walking is possible in the daytime, but prepare for heat and sun.
You can visit at any time of year, and if you will be walking, the dry season of
November–May
is more comfortable. In the rainy season sudden showers can come, so bring an umbrella.
Around
March 19
, the Solemnity of St. Joseph and the parish feast, there are many events and the church is lively but crowded. Mass schedules may change in December.

The church itself has no lodging or restaurant. It is easier to take care of meals and lodging around Greenhills Shopping Center and Ortigas Center. Check the latest maps and reviews for specific places.

After Mass you can have lunch at Greenhills Shopping Center or stop by the malls on the Ortigas Center side. The area around the church is residential and has few restaurants, so it is better to settle on lunch near the shopping center.
Mass times are 7:15 AM and 6:15 PM on weekdays, and on Sundays 6:00 AM (Tagalog) and several Masses from 7:15 AM. Check the latest announcement before you visit.
The Wednesday evening Mass is a votive Mass to St. Joseph and the Friday evening Mass is a votive Mass to the Holy Family.
Confession is reported on Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 5:00 to 6:00 PM.
Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is advisable.
During Mass, do not use flash, keep noise down and do not take photos.
Combining the visit with Greenhills Shopping Center makes your itinerary more efficient.
You can call the parish with inquiries. Check the official announcement for the number.
Church schedules can be found on its Facebook page or website.
This is a working parish, not a tourist attraction. Take care not to disturb Mass or people at prayer.
Mass schedules and events can change without notice.
Parking is unconfirmed, and some reviews say it is tight on busy days, so inquire in advance if you are coming by car.
Keep an eye on your belongings.
On Sundays and feast days it is crowded and getting around can be slow.
Take photos outside Mass times and avoid capturing people's faces.
A major shopping area within walking distance, which also has the Holy Family Chapel under the parish's care.
A business and shopping district reachable by vehicle, with a link to the company that donated the church's land.
A large mall on the Ortigas side; check the travel time locally.
The parish also oversees the Immaculate Conception and Sacred Heart chapels in Crame, San Juan. They are not a special attraction for general travelers, so confirm before visiting.
